```bash
unit_file() {
    case "$1" in
        *.service|*.path) echo "/etc/systemd/system/$1" ;;
        *) echo "/etc/systemd/system/$1.service" ;;
    esac
}
```

`qisutu-install-complete.service` matches `*.service` → `/etc/systemd/system/qisutu-install-complete.service`. OK.

Next, oneshot_run:
- f = that file ✓
- svc = extracted from the line "ExecStart=/bin/systemctl enable --now qisutu-daemon.service" → `qisutu-daemon.service` ✓
- f = /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-daemon.service ✓
- base = qisutu
- state_set daemon-qisutu enabled
- start_daemon qisutu-daemon.service

Inside start_daemon:
- f=/etc/systemd/system/qisutu-daemon.service
- base=qisutu
- pidfile=/run/qisutu/qisutu.pid
- daemon_running check → no pidfile → proceed
- user=$(sed -n 's/^User=//p' f) → qisutu
- group → www-data
- execstart=$(sed -n 's/^ExecStart=//p' f) → /usr/bin/perl /opt/qisutu/bin/qisutu-daemon.pl --sleep 3 --max-jobs 100
- setsid runuser -u qisutu -g www-data -- "execstart" >> log 2>&1 &
- echo $! > pidfile
- sleep 1
- daemon_running → kill -0 pid

Hmm, `echo $!` — $! is the PID of the backgrounded setsid process. But wait: `setsid runuser ... &` — $! is the PID of setsid. setsid might fork (when setsid is called from a process group leader… actually, setsid only forks when it's a process group leader). In a script run from bash, backgrounded jobs are… hmm, in non-interactive bash, job control is off, so background jobs run in the same process group. setsid only calls fork() when getpid() == getpgid(). If the bash script is run from a terminal tool wrapper, then the bash process's pgid is… it's complicated.

The issue is: setsid may fork and create a new session, in which case the original PID dies and the child (the actual daemon) has a different PID. So kill -0 $pid fails → daemon_running returns 1 → start_daemon returns 1.
